title: Geometry - Lesson 5 Practice: Constructing Parallel Lines
description: Practice vocabulary, construction steps, and checks for drawing a parallel line through a point.

questions.question: The symbol $\parallel$ means ______.
questions.explanation: The symbol $\parallel$ is read as 'is parallel to.'

questions.question: You are given line $\ell$ and point $P$ not on the line. What is the goal of the construction?
options: Draw a line through $P$ perpendicular to $\ell$
Draw a line through $P$ parallel to $\ell$
Draw a line segment from $P$ to $\ell$
questions.explanation: The target construction is a line through the given point that has the same direction as the original line.

questions.question: A transversal makes a $52^\circ$ angle with line $\ell$. To construct a parallel through $P$, what corresponding angle should be copied at $P$?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles must be equal, so the copied angle is $52^\circ$.

questions.question: When using a set square to draw a parallel line, rotating the set square slightly is acceptable as long as the new line passes through $P$.
questions.explanation: Rotating changes the direction. The set square must slide without rotating.

questions.question: Which measurement best verifies that two lines are parallel?
options: Two slanted distances between the lines are equal
Two perpendicular distances between the lines are equal
questions.explanation: Parallel lines stay the same perpendicular distance apart.

questions.question: If $m \parallel \ell$, then line $m$ is ______ to line $\ell$.
questions.explanation: $m \parallel \ell$ is read as 'line m is parallel to line ell.'

questions.question: Why does copying a corresponding angle help construct a parallel line?
questions.correctAnswer: If corresponding angles are equal, then the two lines cut by the transversal are parallel.
questions.explanation: The copied angle creates the equal corresponding-angle relationship needed for parallel lines.

questions.question: Describe one accurate method for constructing a line through point $P$ parallel to a given line $\ell$.
questions.correctAnswer: One method is to draw a transversal through P, measure the corresponding angle on line ell, copy that angle at P, and draw the new line through P along the copied angle.
questions.explanation: A complete method names the tools or angle relationship and explains how the new line passes through P.
